mechanism: Targeting-isolation control: keeps the REAL human-observed bursty-v1.1 fire probabilities and volley-size mix (not GA-tuned) and changes ONLY the column choice from random to spawn-first (cols 3,4 then rest). Achieves most of the dies-ahead exploit at the LOWEST average garbage spend of any candidate (27.2 halves), isolating targeting (not timing or volume) as the dominant lever. Was expected a priori to be the most robust candidate (garbage physically raising the spawn-lane floor is a board-geometry fact, not a tuned-policy artifact) -- that expectation did NOT hold. STRUCTURAL-FILTER VERDICT: FLUKE (2/5 perturbation categories survived -- [a] neighbouring-seeds=True, timing_jitter=True; [b] history-shift=False, column_jitter=False, size_jitter=False -- below the >=3/5 majority bar). Even the targeting-only isolation, with the real human-observed timing/size shape held fixed, does not reliably beat the honest baseline off its own original n=120 seed block. This is the most important negative in this document: ALL THREE of Hunt B's dies-ahead candidates (this one plus both ga_near_spawn_* genomes) failed the structural filter -- the n=120 holdout's non-overlapping CIs were real but seed-block-specific, not evidence of a general champion weakness.
